blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Work on efficient large-language-model inference has concentrated almost entirely on reducing the cost of decoding once a request is complete. The quantity a user experiences, however, is the interval between submitting a request and receiving a usable response, and that interval can be shortened without making decoding itself faster. While a request is being composed it is already partially specified, yet conventional deployments begin no computation until submission. We propose and study streaming generation, a decoding regime in which the model begins producing a response from an incomplete request and revises it as the remaining input arrives, so that only a small residue of the answer remains to be computed once the request is submitted. We evaluate the regime on autoregressive and diffusion language models, characterise the conditions under which it reduces user-visible latency, and analyse the mechanism responsible.
blocks.zh: 关于高效的大语言模型推论的工作几乎完全集中在一旦请求完成后降低解码费用上. 然而,用户经历的数量是提交请求和收到可用答复之间的间隔,而这一间隔可以缩短,而不会使自己解码更快。 虽然一项请求正在编写中,但已经部分具体说明,但常规部署直到提交后才开始计算。 我们提议并研究流化生成,这是一种编解码制度,即模型开始从不完整的请求中产生答复,并在剩余输入到达时加以修订,这样,在提交请求后,只有一小部分答案尚待计算。 我们评价关于自动递减和传播语言模式的制度,确定减少用户可见延迟的条件,并分析负责的机制。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Research on efficient large-language-model inference optimizes the cost of
producing a response once the request is known, and identifies that cost with the
user’s waiting time. This identification is valid only under the convention that decoding begins at
submission. Composing a request takes several seconds, during which the
request is already partially specified and the model performs no work. Streaming
generation uses that interval: the model drafts a response from the partial request
and revises the draft as the remainder arrives, so that little work remains once
the user submits.

The regime changes the quantity to be measured. Total decoding cost ceases to be
the appropriate objective, because computation performed before the user finishes
composing is not part of the observed latency. We therefore measure the residual cost: the forward passes and wall-clock time required after the
final token of the request becomes available.

blocks.en:
• We formalise streaming generation and adopt residual cost as the evaluation
criterion, and give a single draft–verify–regenerate procedure that
instantiates it for both autoregressive and diffusion decoders. • We evaluate the regime on six benchmarks spanning the tasks an assistant is
actually asked to perform: program synthesis from a specification (HumanEval,
MBPP), data-science code completion (DS-1000), instructed code editing
(CanItEdit), text editing (CoEdIT) and multi-turn dialogue. • On a slot-based diffusion model with an autoregressive verifier
(ReFusion-8B, Li et al., 2025b ) the procedure lowers residual cost by 2.18 × 2.18\times in forward passes and 1.88 × 1.88\times in wall clock, averaged over
the six benchmarks, without significant loss in quality. The gain is largest
where the opening of the request already determines the answer, reaching 4.67 × 4.67\times and 3.68 × 3.68\times on HumanEval. • On three autoregressive models the same procedure yields macro-averaged median
residual speedups of 14.4 × 14.4\times (Gemma-3-12B), 1.23 × 1.23\times (Llama-3.1-8B)
and 1.21 × 1.21\times (Qwen3-8B), at an average quality drop of 2.8 2.8 to 6.1 6.1 points across the six benchmarks. • We show that the procedure does not transfer to fully bidirectional diffusion
models (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B), and explain why. Verification there asks the model
to judge tokens that it can see, which it will almost always approve: offered a
draft answering a completely different question, it accepts every token. What
the method needs is a verifier whose judgement of a token is formed without
access to that token, at a cost that does not grow with the length of the
answer. Causal attention provides exactly this in a single forward pass. • We report that self-distillation on incomplete requests helps, and that what it
buys differs by model. On Qwen3-8B it roughly doubles the mean residual speedup
( 11.9 → 24.8 × 11.9\to 24.8\times ) and raises the median by a third
( 1.21 → 1.65 × 1.21\to 1.65\times ), by lengthening the drafts the verifier already accepts.
On Gemma-3-12B, which streams well to begin with, it adds a little of both
accuracy and speed. On ReFusion-8B it improves accuracy by up to 17 17 points.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by having a cheap
drafter propose several tokens that the target model verifies in a single parallel
forward pass, provably preserving the target distribution ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) . Follow-up work mostly addresses the
cost and fidelity of the drafter: Medusa attaches lightweight parallel decoding
heads to a frozen backbone ( Cai et al., 2024 ) , self-speculative decoding drafts
by skipping intermediate layers of the target model itself ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) ,
and EAGLE autoregresses over hidden features rather than tokens ( Li et al., 2024 ) ; Xia et al. (2024) survey the area. These methods share when the draft is produced and from what : speculation occurs at decode
time, after the request is complete, and the draft originates from a smaller,
early-exiting or auxiliary head. Our setting differs on both counts. The draft is
produced by the same model during composition, so speculative computation occupies
an interval that would otherwise go unused and no auxiliary drafter must be trained
or deployed. Verification at submission serves the function that parallel
verification serves in speculative decoding, but the accepted prefix is carried
across a turn boundary rather than across a few decode steps.

blocks.en:
Beginning work before the input is complete is not a new idea, although we are
not aware of prior work in the typed-text setting. Its oldest form is simultaneous
translation, where wait- k k policies emit target tokens from a source prefix ( Ma et al., 2019 ) and re-translation revises the hypothesis as the source grows ( Arivazhagan et al., 2020 ) ; SSBD makes re-translation efficient by reusing
the previous output as a self-speculative draft for the extended input ( Zeng et al., 2025 ) . In speech, PredGen performs “input-time
speculation”, drafting a response from the first ASR chunk and refining it as later
chunks arrive ( Li and Grover, 2025 ) ; it is the closest neighbour to this work,
differing in modality and in using standard autoregressive speculative decoding.
Outside language, SpeQL begins executing a SQL query before the user has finished
typing it ( Li et al., 2025a ) .

blocks.en:
Discrete diffusion for text was placed on a principled footing by D3PM ( Austin et al., 2021a ) and later simplified: Sahoo et al. (2024) show that
a Rao-Blackwellized masked-diffusion objective reduces to a mixture of masked-LM
losses. Scaling the recipe yields general-purpose diffusion LLMs such as LLaDA ( Nie et al., 2025 ) and, through semi-autoregressive and block decoding,
practically deployable variants ( Han et al., 2023 ; Arriola et al., 2025 ) . The relevant
property is that every position in the current window is re-predicted at each step,
so an already-emitted token may be revised rather than being frozen, as it
necessarily is under autoregressive decoding.

因此,一个已经得到的代币可以修改而不是冻结,因为它

blocks.en:
Our principal diffusion backbone is ReFusion-8B ( Li et al., 2025b ) , which differs
from the models above in two respects that the method depends on. First, its answer buffer is divided into
fixed-size slots , and a slot is committed only when the model’s confidence in
its contents exceeds a threshold; decoding therefore terminates as soon as the
answer is complete rather than after a fixed number of denoising steps. Second, and critically for this work, its attention is causal and it is trained with
a mixed objective: an
autoregressive loss on committed positions and a masked-diffusion loss on masked
ones. The model consequently exposes two predictors for the same buffer. The
diffusion predictor fills masked slots in place; the autoregressive predictor scores
a token from the state to its left, which cannot observe the token itself. The
second is what makes verification meaningful, and its absence is what we will show
prevents the method from transferring to fully bidirectional diffusion models.
Closest in spirit is SpecDiff ( Christopher et al., 2025 ) , which uses a
discrete diffusion model as a parallel drafter verified by an autoregressive model;
we likewise pair masked diffusion with an autoregressive verifier, but both roles
are played by a single model and the verified content is carried across turns.

blocks.en:
A large body of systems work accelerates inference by caching key-value state across
requests: Prompt Cache precomputes attention states for reusable prompt modules ( Gim et al., 2024 ) , SGLang’s RadixAttention maintains a radix tree over KV caches
so that shared prefixes are matched automatically ( Zheng et al., 2024b ) ,
PagedAttention supplies the memory substrate that makes such sharing practical ( Kwon et al., 2023 ) , and CacheBlend relaxes the strict-prefix requirement by
selectively recomputing a small subset of tokens ( Yao et al., 2025 ) . What
unifies them is what is reused: the computation belongs to the request, so
they shorten prefill. We reuse the answer computed while the user was still
composing, and therefore save decode rather than prefill; the two are composable.

Latency is conventionally decomposed into time-to-first-token and
time-per-output-token, and systems work optimizes both: Orca introduces

to remove decode stalls ( Agrawal et al., 2024 ) , and DistServe disaggregates
prefill from decode to meet the two targets independently ( Zhong et al., 2024 ) .
All of them start the clock at submission, which is the assumption relaxed here.

blocks.en: 3 Streaming Generation
blocks.zh: 3 流化生成

blocks.en:
The granularity at which a partially composed request becomes available depends on
the application and the domain. A code
assistant may observe every keystroke; a chat interface may see text arrive in
bursts; a voice interface receives transcription chunks whose boundaries are set by
the recogniser. No single segmentation is universally appropriate. We therefore adopt an explicit
simplification: composition is modelled as the arrival of successive sentences ,
and each sentence boundary is treated as a point at which new input becomes
available. This is a controlled proxy for keystroke-level composition, selected
because it is reproducible across benchmarks and because a sentence is the smallest
unit after which a request is generally interpretable.

The two families differ only in step 3. An autoregressive decoder writes strictly
left to right and cannot go back, so it simply resumes writing after the accepted

difference is that the diffusion model is free to change its mind about text it has
already written, and the autoregressive model is not.

blocks.en: 6.3 Where it works, and why

blocks.en:
Streaming pays off when the request is of the form “produce an artefact from a
specification”. The specification appears in the opening sentences, and what follows
is illustration (examples, assertions, formatting markers) that refines the answer
without changing its structure. The draft written from the first sentence is
then already close to the final answer, it survives each update, and at submission
only a verification pass and a short remainder are left. HumanEval and MBPP are of
this form, and both families behave the same way on them: the diffusion model reaches 4.67 × 4.67\times and 3.33 × 3.33\times , and the strongest autoregressive checkpoint reaches 74 × 74\times on MBPP.

rephrasing fails a token-level acceptance test, so drafts are discarded even when they
were perfectly good answers. Chat sits at the bottom of the table for this reason
rather than because its requests are hard.

The two observations are the same observation. An autoregressive decoder cannot
revise a token it has emitted, so whatever part of the draft is accepted is fixed for
good, including the part that was written before the request was complete. Where

because it re-predicts every position in its buffer and can revise an accepted
region if the completed request calls for it. The quality cost of streaming is
therefore not intrinsic to the regime. It is the price of irreversible decoding, and
it is paid only by the family that decodes irreversibly.

blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
Time to answer, rather than decoding latency, is what a user experiences, and it can
be reduced without making decoding faster. Streaming generation does so on both
decoder families we studied. On the diffusion model it removes 37.6 % 37.6\% of the forward passes a user waits
through. On the two benchmarks whose opening already determines the answer it is 4.67 × 4.67\times and 3.33 × 3.33\times cheaper in forward passes and 3.68 × 3.68\times and 2.90 × 2.90\times faster in wall clock, at quality that is unchanged on HumanEval and two
points higher on MBPP. On the autoregressive side the gain is larger still where the
model commits early: Gemma-3-12B reaches a median of 74 × 74\times on MBPP and finishes
a third of all requests in a single forward pass after submission. Adapting a model
to incomplete requests raises the gain further, roughly doubling the mean on
Qwen3-8B.

Two properties decide whether a model can do this. Its verifier must be able to
reject a stale draft, which requires that a token be judged without being seen;
causal attention supplies this in one forward pass, and full bidirectional attention
does not supply it at all. And because a rejected draft costs one verification pass
while an accepted one saves work in proportion to the length of the answer, streaming
is worth applying to every request rather than to a selected few. The computation it
spends is computation that would otherwise sit idle while the user is still typing.

blocks.en:
The regime trades throughput for the latency of an individual user, and the exchange
rate should be stated. Streaming regenerates the answer at every sentence, so total
forward passes rise by a factor of 1.3 1.3 to 5.4 5.4 across the diffusion benchmarks,
and by 3.5 3.5 to 3.9 3.9 on the two where the residual gain is largest. The
autoregressive side likewise performs speculative work during composition
that residual metrics do not charge. This work is done while the accelerator would
otherwise be idle, so the method suits interactive or local deployment and is not
intended for a saturated batch system.
